reviewer.method: Read the complete actual text for every case and judged its meaning against the supplied business scenario, context, and review questions. Consulted implementation for memory constraints and storage failure handling. No keyword, regular-expression, fixed-sentence, snapshot, or source-snippet match was used to decide semantic acceptance. Prior reported verdicts were not adopted as evidence.

provenance.revisionScope: Review of the working-tree change based on this revision. The owning change must retain the fixture and source contents identified below; the base revision alone is not a claim that it contains the uncommitted edits.

fixture.generationResult: 20 cases emitted with pending verdicts. An independent regeneration at review time reproduced all 20 complete evidence objects exactly. Comparing their identity only established which already-read materials were recreated; it did not decide their meaning.
fixture.runtimeLimitation: The observed Node runtime is outside the repository engine requirement >=24.5 <25. The fixture completed, but this review makes no supported-engine runtime acceptance claim.

provenance.hashPolicy: SHA256 values identify the exact UTF-8 actualText bytes (without normalization), emitted JSON bytes, fixture generator, and relevant source bytes. They are provenance only: no digest decides meaning, accepts later output, or turns a fresh pending generation into a pass. New or changed semantic output requires subjective review even if an older record passed.
provenance.durability: No temporary directory is a long-term evidence dependency. Recreate cases from the fixture at the reviewed source contents retained with this change, select each case by id, and consult the per-case rationale and scope. The generated text is deliberately not stored here as a golden snapshot.

cases.rationale: The control manual gives usable choices among dialog, task, and agent reminders, distinguishes Taskdoc current truth from durable memory, and keeps long evidence in formal documents with pointers. It explains preserving goals and volatile details before clearing, with the side-dialog degraded-context exception taking precedence over generic Taskdoc editing advice. The reply-routing rules separate executor delegation, necessary ask-back, human intervention, and exact reply-tool completion without treating responsibility as a grant.

cases.rationale: The recovery guidance accurately distinguishes existing-path add failures, missing-path replace/delete failures, invalid input, and filesystem failures. It rejects invented error catalogs and fixed storage limits, asks the agent to inspect uncertain writes before repeating them, and preserves the automatic personal namespace and the consequence of clearing the member store. mem.ts supplies structured input/existence failures, while the driver converts thrown storage exceptions into failure outcomes with the actual error.
cases.scope: Full English personal_memory errors chapter cross-checked against mem.ts, toolFailure in tool.ts, and the tool execution exception boundary in kernel-driver/drive.ts. No storage fault was injected and no filesystem capacity or platform limit was measured.

assertionReview.scope: Complete tracked test diff against HEAD plus full untracked tests/run.mjs, tests/runner.test.mjs, and tests/semantic/evidence.ts, as read in this review. Includes the surrounding assertions in modified tests, deleted scripts, package entrypoints, and test README. This review record itself adds no acceptance code.

items.rationale: Changed synchronization observes persisted generation-start and queued-input events instead of elapsed time. Assertions establish queue consumption, input order, absence of a separate guide record, and visible delivery of the mock answer. The wrapped text is generated once and used as a fixture payload; equality checks byte-preserving placement of that supplied input, not whether its remediation prose has the right meaning. finalAnswer and seedPrompt are fixed mock data, not natural-language semantic oracles.

The provider mock switches on a distinct input msgId rather than recognizing the recovery instruction by English wording. Assertions inspect retry count, persisted diligence_push origin, linkage of the persisted prompt identity to generator context, and exactly one human answer carrying the fixed mock payload. RECOVERED_TEXT equality checks delivery integrity. It cannot establish semantic quality of the actual recovery prompt, and the test does not claim that.

Added fixture dispatch state establishes the actual parent/callee relationship needed for a reply; a separate mainline root prevents unrelated unconsumed replies from contaminating the residue scenario. Explicitly queuing the injected stale trigger causes the backend path to be exercised. Assertions compare stored trigger state, consumed batch identity, and generation counts, while fixed mock response equality shows the expected result reached the right caller. Those sentences are transport payloads chosen by the test, not quality judgments about generated language.

The new deep equality specifies actual metadata data: provider/model identifiers and the configured-model-id field for a registered external API type with no built-in parameter namespace. Existing description/default-label strings in this file come from a supplied providerConfig fixture and are tested for faithful propagation, not for natural-language meaning. Structured JSON value equality protects serialization.

Exit status order, counters, exit code, summary serialization, retained timeout evidence, success cleanup, discovery paths, and a long descriptive case path are machine/process contracts. The two regex checks look only for constant sentinel bytes emitted by subprocess fixtures created in this same test; they establish failure log retention and that a later case ran despite earlier failures. They do not inspect prose from a prompt, manual, guidance, or explanation. The long-name case executes the real tsx boundary and asserts process success.

The runner has no semantic acceptance assertion. Its regexes parse package-script grammar, sanitize case filenames, and discover TypeScript entrypoints; its status is determined by child exit/timeout, not output keywords such as PASS. Helpers/evidence generators are excluded from kernel candidate passes, cases run sequentially, failures/timeouts preserve state, the suite reports all attempted normal cases and sets a nonzero exit status for failure/timeout. This source review does not prove platform-specific process-tree cleanup or every I/O failure path.

The fixture emits complete actual text plus business scenario, context, questions, and a per-case pending review manifest. It performs no wording assertions and never loads this report to automatically accept output. Fixed case IDs and modes name the scenario. Successful generation is explicitly distinct from semantic acceptance; this report records the separately performed subjective review.
